gates.fresh_problem: Take two genuinely different Doré directions for the same fresh brief. Compare them on one declared primary axis, hold accessibility and technical quality constant, select a winner, and preserve both winner and loser reasons with project-specific evidence.
acceptance: comparison context is explicit
primary axis is singular and meaningful
winner and loser reasons are both retained
brand fit and usability floor are assessed separately
evidence references retained
preference scope is declared
gates.next_action: Write the comparison to taste memory as scoped precedent, not a universal rule.

gates.fresh_problem: Review three previously rejected or abandoned Doré UI directions. For each, determine whether the rejection reason is local, surface-family specific, or genuinely reusable. Produce compact warnings without converting local failures into global bans.
acceptance: at least three rejection cases are examined
each rejection has a reason and scope
local and reusable lessons are distinguished
no rejection becomes a global ban without repeated evidence
contradictory evidence is retained
gates.next_action: Persist only the reusable warning plus scope and evidence; leave local rejections local.

gates.fresh_problem: Critique a live Doré surface using two independent channels: A design-director judgment and B deterministic/runtime evidence. Keep B hidden from A until A is complete, then synthesize agreements, disagreements, false positives, and unresolved items.
acceptance: two independent assessment channels exist
design assessment completes before detector evidence is synthesized
agreements and disagreements are explicit
detector false positives may be rejected with reasons
runtime PASS cannot substitute for visual PASS
severity-ranked fixes are concrete
gates.next_action: Use unresolved disagreements as targeted follow-up tests rather than averaging them away.

gates.fresh_problem: Extract a compact Doré motion vocabulary from existing successful and failed interactions. For each motion term, define semantic purpose, trigger, enter/settle/exit behavior, interruption/reversal rule, reduced-motion equivalent, and at least one project example or counterexample.
acceptance: motion terms are named consistently
semantic purpose is separate from implementation
interruption and return are defined
reduced-motion equivalent is defined
project examples or counterexamples are retained
vocabulary remains compact
gates.next_action: Use named motion contracts in the next real interaction patch instead of vague adjectives.

gates.fresh_problem: Given a new Doré UI problem, retrieve only the smallest set of context-near taste comparisons, rejection warnings, and motion precedents. Use them as precedent rather than authority, then make a fresh decision and state whether any prior preference is reversed.
acceptance: retrieval is context-filtered and bounded
irrelevant history is excluded
precedent is not copied as a template
fresh evidence can override memory
preference reversal is recorded explicitly when it occurs
prompt/history size does not grow with total memory
gates.next_action: Run this retrieval on a surface outside Candidate 1 and compare against a no-memory control.

gates.fresh_problem: On a completely fresh Doré surface, make one consequential visual or interaction decision using bounded precedent retrieval. Produce at least two viable alternatives, reject one with scoped reasons, implement or specify the winner, dual-channel critique it, and then write the outcome back as compact taste memory. The task must permit reversal of prior precedent.
acceptance: fresh surface is outside training examples
retrieval is bounded
two viable alternatives are compared
winner and rejection reasons are evidence-backed
dual-channel critique passes or blocks promotion explicitly
prior precedent may be reversed
new memory is compact and scoped
no global style lock-in is introduced
gates.next_action: Promote Taste Memory III only after a blind fresh-surface run demonstrates transfer without copying.
